attempted_claim: Let K be algebraically closed of characteristic zero, R=K[x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4], S=K[X_1,...,X_4], and A_F=R/Ann_R(F) a graded Artinian Gorenstein algebra of codimension 4 with Macaulay dual generator F in S_d, h-vector h and Sperner number S_A=max h_i. Find a necessary and sufficient condition on F (equivalently on h plus Macaulay-dual data) for existence of a zero-dimensional scheme Z in P^3 of length S_A with I(Z) subset Ann_R(F) — a tight annihilating scheme, equivalently A_F is a doubling 0 -> omega_{R/I(Z)}(-d) -> R/I(Z) -> A_F -> 0 — extending the Iarrobino-Kanev / Miro-Roig codimension-3 criterion; in particular determine whether N_{S_A}>=3 (three consecutive peaks attaining S_A) suffices in codimension 4, and when the condition holds deduce the weak Lefschetz property, the mapping-cone minimal free resolution from that of R/I(Z), and the generic Jordan type from mixed Hessians of F.
decisive_failure: No theorem is claimed. Exact rational-rank computations cover only finitely many sampled dual generators (degrees 5-6); the N>=3 sufficiency question, the general tight-scheme criterion, and the conditional WLP/resolution/Jordan-type deductions are all left open. Artifacts document the computational engine and negative search results for reproducibility.
